mechanism: The same aggregate positive fraction may arise from locally balanced variables or from a mixture of strongly one-sided variables. Mean per-variable polarity imbalance distinguishes those cases while positive-literal fraction remains the directional anchor. This tests whether routing benefits require a particular distribution of signed constraints, using two existing features and no new derived quantity.

proposal.hypothesis: A global positive-literal fraction can conceal different distributions of polarity across variables. Test the existing mean per-variable polarity imbalance as a conditioning feature for the existing signed preference, rather than another unsigned density or clause-size proxy. Fit alone chooses thresholds and actions.
